errors.problem: The engine transliterates the relative pronouns الَّذِي / الَّتِي / الَّذِينَ as 'Illadhī', 'illatī', 'illadhīna' whenever they are not preceded by a vowel (titles, lists, quiz options, after a consonant: 'ṣadīq illadhī'). The lām carries shadda+fatḥa and no sukūn, so the engine does not recognise the article and treats the alif as hamzat waṣl with -i-. The correct pronunciation is alladhī / allatī / alladhīna (the 'why' text of d74s1 itself says 'alladhī'). Inside sentences after a vowel ('r-rajulu lladhī') the output is right.
errors.fix: alladhī / allatī / alladhīna (engine rule: الَّ at the start of a word = al-l…, not il-l…)
errors.alsoChange: the same affects every isolated occurrence of these three words in day 74 and the Week 11 completion text of day 77

errors.problem: The engine transliterates الِاجْتِمَاعِيِّ (article before a word beginning with hamzat waṣl, written with kasra on the lām) as 'liājtimāʿiyyi' / 'liājtimāʿī'. Correct: l-ijtimāʿiyyi (after t-tawāṣuli), i.e. 'wasāʾilu t-tawāṣuli l-ijtimāʿiyyi'. The Arabic is right; only the transliteration is wrong, but the learner reads a non-existent word in a key vocabulary item (social media).
errors.fix: wasāʾilu t-tawāṣuli l-ijtimāʿiyyi (engine rule: الِ + alif-waṣl = al-i…, article vowel elided after a vowel)

errors.problem: The engine fails on بِ + article after وَ: وَبِالْحَيَوَانَاتِ وَبِالْأَشْجَار comes out as 'wabiālḥayawānāti wabiālʾashjār' instead of 'wa-bi-l-ḥayawānāti wa-bi-l-ashjār'. Elsewhere بِالْ alone is handled correctly ('bi-l-ʿīd', 'bi-ṣ-ṣiḥḥati'), so the bug is the وَبِالْ stack. The Arabic is correct.

'Today is Thursday' is a nominal sentence whose subject is الْيَوْمُ; it needs the nominative -u. With the fatḥa (الْيَوْمَ) the word is the adverb 'today' and the sentence has no subject. The learner hears 'al-yawma l-khamīs' for a pattern the course has been teaching with -u (d73 objective 3, 'hear the case endings').
errors.alsoChange: seg gloss stays 'today'; transliteration becomes 'Al-yawmu l-khamīs' automatically

errors.current: تُعْطِي=you give (to a woman); she gives
errors.problem: Tap gloss gives the wrong form: تُعْطِي is 'you (m) give' (indicative) or 'she gives'. 'You give (to a woman)' is تُعْطِينَ. The gloss is attached to the very contrast the lesson teaches (tuʿṭī indicative vs tuʿṭi jussive), so a learner will take تُعْطِي as a feminine form.
errors.fix: تُعْطِي=you give (to a man, statement); she gives

errors.problem: The tap glosses of the إِنَّ family are fixed to one sense regardless of context. In day 73 the lesson teaches إِنَّ as the statement-opener 'indeed' (the segs say 'indeed'), but every tap shows 'that (after 'say')'. Conversely in day 75, where إِنَّهَا means 'that she' after قَالَتْ, the tap shows 'إِنَّهَا=indeed it (f) ('it is')' (intro, objectives[3], d75s2 right, d75q3 option 1). Learners tapping the quiz options in d73q3 and d75q3 get a gloss that contradicts the lesson.
errors.fix: day 73 taps: إِنَّ=indeed; that (after 'say') — day 75 taps: إِنَّهَا=that she (after qāla); indeed she/it
errors.alsoChange: إِنَّهَا tap 'indeed it (f) ('it is')' in day 75 intro, objectives[3], sentences[1].mistakes[0].right, quiz[2].options[1]

errors.problem: In أَعْرِفُ أَنَّهَا تُحِبُّ الْمُوسِيقَى the verb is 'she loves' (the sentence seg says 'she loves'); the tap gloss shows only the 2nd-person masculine sense, which contradicts the sentence and the 'why' text (annahā … she).
errors.fix: تُحِبُّ=she loves; you like (to a man)

errors.problem: In أَعْلَنَتِ الْحُكُومَةُ عُطْلَةً the -an is the object ending (the sentence seg says 'a holiday'), not a predicate after كَانَ. The tap gloss imports a rule from another lesson and misleads the learner about why the word ends in -an.

errors.current: أَنْتَ=you (written without vowel marks: anta or anti)
errors.problem: The word in the quiz is fully vowelled (أَنْتَ, 'to a man'); the tap gloss says it is unvowelled and could be anti. Wrong statement about the form shown.

حِمَايَةُ is the maṣdar 'protection / protecting (of)', not a verb 'protects'; the dialogue seg (d78l14) glosses it correctly as 'protecting, protection (of)'. The objective is exactly where the lesson introduces verbal nouns, so the gloss teaches the wrong word class.
Known engine quirk: a final ي with no vowel mark is rendered as long ī, so رَأْي (raʾy) appears as 'Raʾī'. The Arabic is correct.

notes.note: بَلْ تَعْنِي: كُلُّ شَخْص — as the object of تَعْنِي the phrase would be accusative كُلَّ شَخْصٍ (compare d77l11 'الضِّيقُ يَعْنِي الْوَقْتَ الصَّعْب', which uses the accusative). The colon makes a quoted-gloss reading possible, so not counted as an error; consider كُلَّ شَخْص for consistency.

لَازِم أَنْ is colloquial/semi-formal rather than fuṣḥā; MSA writing uses يَجِبُ أَنْ or مِنَ اللَّازِمِ أَنْ. Acceptable in dialogue, but presenting it as a parallel MSA structure in the objectives is a register choice the owner may want to flag.
سَأَلَنِي … هَلْ … is understood but formal MSA more often reports a yes/no question with إِنْ كُنْتُ / إِذَا كُنْتُ or عَمَّا إِذَا. Register note only.

إِنْ دَرَسْتَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، نَجَحْتَ … is correct classical past-past conditional, but the apodosis in the past sounds archaic for a beginner; modern MSA would say فَسَتَنْجَحُ (as the course itself does with فَسَنَزُورُ). Style only.
بِخَيْر is tagged 'adj'; it is a preposition + noun (bi + khayr). Harmless for the learner but inconsistent with the pos labels elsewhere.
Tap gloss 'أَعْلَنَ=announces (past)' is self-contradictory; '(he) announced' would be clearer.
Grammar tag 'numbers-11-100' on خَمْسَ سَاعَاتٍ (a 3–10 number). Tag only, not learner-visible content.
Intro says خَاصّ means 'private' but the tap gloss shows 'special'; both are valid senses, and the dialogue (مَعْلُومَاتِنَا الْخَاصَّة) uses 'private'. Consider 'private; special' in the tap.
حَتَّى أَبُوكُمَا after لِأَيِّ شَخْصٍ: nominative is defensible (ḥattā ibtidāʾiyya, 'even your father [is included]'); the coordinating reading would give أَبِيكُمَا. Not an error.
صَلَاة rendered 'Ṣalāh' (ة in pause as -h) while elsewhere ة is '-a' (ʿīdiyya, ḥafla). Transliteration consistency only.

summary: Read the whole export for days 71–80 (2,829 lines): every Arabic string with its harakat and case endings, agreement, verb forms and moods after أَنْ/لَنْ/لَمْ, the English and literal translations, every seg and tap gloss, all quiz answer keys and all mistakes right/wrong pairs, and the transliteration against the Arabic. The Arabic itself is in very good shape: the case work the week teaches (إِنَّ/أَنَّ/لٰكِنَّ + accusative, kāna + -an, lām of the apodosis after لَوْ, fa- before sa-, numbers 3–10 with gender reversal, duals, the relative pronouns) is consistently correct, and every answer key checked out. I found one genuine case slip (الْيَوْمَ الْخَمِيس for 'today is Thursday'). The real problems are in the engine and the tap-gloss layer: the relative pronoun is transliterated 'Illadhī' in every isolated position in day 74 (major, repeated ~15 times), the article before a hamzat-waṣl word (الِاجْتِمَاعِيّ) and the وَبِالْ stack produce garbage transliterations, and several tap glosses are context-blind (إِنَّ 'that (after say)' shown where the lesson teaches 'indeed', إِنَّهَا 'indeed it' shown where it means 'that she', تُحِبُّ 'you like' for 'she loves', تُعْطِي labelled 'to a woman', عُطْلَةً '(after was)', حِمَايَةُ 'protects'). Totals: 13 errors (4 major: 3 engine, 1 gloss; 9 minor: 1 arabic, 5 gloss, 3 engine), 10 notes.
